article.headline: Inside Aschenbrenner's AGI Fund: What Moved and What Held
article.lede: Tweet 4/6 in a thread from @BlackPantherCap dissects what Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness LP likely did with its holdings in its latest quarterly 13F filing. Aschenbrenner, a 25-year-old former OpenAI researcher who launched the fund in September 2024, runs a concentrated book organized around a single mandate: find the physical constraint that capital cannot route around, and buy the company that controls it. The analysis separates probable profit-taking from structural conviction holds.
article.body:
Situational Awareness LP entered 2026 with a disclosed U.S. equity book of roughly $5.5–7 billion spread across fewer than 30 stocks — a concentration that makes each position a deliberate thesis, not a hedge. The fund's defining posture is anti-consensus: it exited Nvidia (NVDA) and Broadcom (AVGO) early, dismissing both as too widely owned, and instead concentrated in the physical substrate of *AGI* — power generation, optical interconnects, *NAND flash* memory, and former bitcoin-mining facilities repurposed as compute campuses.

BlackPantherCap's analysis identifies three probable trims. Bloom Energy (BE) — which sells *solid-oxide fuel cells*, electrochemical devices that convert natural gas or hydrogen into electricity on-site without combustion — is flagged as likely partially trimmed after a gain the poster places at 191% year-to-date. (Calendar-year 2026 data is somewhat murkier; the stock's 52-week run from a 2025 trough near $17 to an all-time high above $310 is extraordinary by any standard, but the exact YTD figure depends heavily on the measurement date and reference price.) SanDisk (SNDK), a pure-play NAND flash memory company spun off from Western Digital (WDC) in February 2025, ran roughly 816% over the trailing twelve months on surging AI-infrastructure storage demand — making some profit-taking, as the poster notes, basic *portfolio hygiene*. The most technically interesting item involves Intel (INTC) call options: if those were exercised into direct shares during the Q1 2026 rally, the 13F would reclassify the line from "call" to "SH" (shares held), and outside observers parsing the filing could misread a conversion as a new purchase — a subtle distinction the analysis flags explicitly.

The held positions carry a different logic. Lumentum Holdings (LITE) is treated as untouchable because Nvidia structurally locked its supply chain in March 2026: Nvidia invested $2 billion in LITE alongside a multi-year purchase commitment for *co-packaged optics* — advanced assemblies that place laser and photodetector components directly inside AI switch packages, slashing networking power consumption by as much as 40% and enabling far denser bandwidth. Simultaneously, Nvidia made an identical $2 billion investment in Coherent (COHR), cementing a two-supplier photonics duopoly at the heart of next-generation AI factory interconnects. Selling a structural position after that kind of procurement commitment, BlackPantherCap argues, is a category error — Nvidia has effectively pre-contracted the supply chain.

IREN Limited (IREN), Core Scientific (CORZ), and Cipher Digital (CIFR) are grouped as "AI compute campuses" — former bitcoin miners that converted power-dense, low-cost-energy facilities into *GPU colocation* and hyperscaler data center hosting. Core Scientific pivoted after emerging from bankruptcy in January 2024, signing 12-year agreements with CoreWeave (CRWV) for 590 megawatts of capacity worth over $10 billion in contracted revenue, then raising $3.3 billion in *high-yield bonds* in April 2026 to fund further buildout across a three-gigawatt pipeline. BlackPantherCap treats all three as early-innings bets on the scarcest AI resource — energized, contracted power — whose thesis, the analysis concludes, is not yet close to played out.

concepts.definition: A quarterly disclosure that U.S. institutional investment managers with over $100 million in assets must file with the SEC, listing their long equity positions as of the quarter-end date. It does not show short positions, unexercised options, or non-equity holdings, making it an incomplete — and frequently misread — snapshot of a fund's actual book.

A hypothetical level of machine intelligence capable of performing any intellectual task a human can, across arbitrary domains, without task-specific training. Distinguished from today's narrow AI systems — which excel at specific tasks but fail outside their training distribution — by genuine generality. The timeline for AGI is fiercely debated; Situational Awareness LP is explicitly premised on its arrival this decade.

An electrochemical device that generates electricity by oxidizing a fuel — typically natural gas or hydrogen — across a ceramic electrolyte, without combustion. Produces lower emissions than gas turbines, generates negligible NOx, and can operate entirely off-grid. AI data centers prize them for dispatchable, grid-independent power at scale.

A type of non-volatile semiconductor storage that retains data without power by trapping electric charge in floating-gate transistors. The dominant technology in solid-state drives, smartphones, and data center storage arrays. AI training and inference workloads require vast amounts of fast, high-density NAND to store model weights, datasets, and intermediate activations.

Informal term for routine position management — trimming holdings that have grown outsized relative to their original thesis weight, taking profits after extreme runs, or reducing exposure where the risk/reward has shifted. The goal is to prevent any single position from dominating the book in a way the manager did not intend, regardless of conviction.

An advanced photonic integration approach that places optical components — lasers, modulators, photodetectors — inside the same chip package as a high-speed network switch or AI accelerator, rather than in a separate pluggable module. Reducing the electrical connection distance from centimeters to millimeters cuts power consumption by up to 40% and enables much higher bandwidth density, which is critical as AI clusters scale to hundreds of thousands of GPUs.

A data center business model in which an operator builds and manages the physical facility — power infrastructure, cooling, networking — and leases space and capacity to clients who own or deploy GPU clusters. Former bitcoin miners are advantaged here because they already control high-power-density sites with established energy contracts and grid connections.

Corporate debt rated below investment grade (below BBB– by S&P or Baa3 by Moody's), also called junk bonds. They carry higher interest rates to compensate for greater default risk. Companies in capital-intensive buildout phases — like AI data center operators converting from crypto mining — frequently issue high-yield debt to fund infrastructure before revenues are fully established.

When a fund holds call options on a stock and exercises them to receive the underlying shares, the position type changes from 'call' to 'SH' (shares held) in the subsequent 13F filing. Outside observers parsing the filing may interpret this shift as a new long position being opened, when it actually represents a conversion of an existing derivative into direct equity — no net new capital deployed.

article.fact_check: The '191% YTD' figure for Bloom Energy (BE) is imprecise. Calendar-year 2026 data places the stock's year-to-date gain through mid-May 2026 somewhere between approximately 70% and 165% depending on source and snapshot date — the wide range reflects BE's extreme volatility and the difficulty of pinning a clean January 1 reference price. The figure may represent Aschenbrenner's entry-price return rather than strict calendar-year performance. The '816% 1Y' figure for SanDisk (SNDK) is broadly consistent with a trailing-twelve-month window from approximately May 2025 (when SNDK was trading near $155 after its February spinoff) to May 2026 prices above $1,400; the figure is not wrong per se, but the stock's actual one-year return by some calculations is significantly higher still, depending on the precise baseline date used.
article.thread_summary: This is tweet 4/6 in a thread by @BlackPantherCap analyzing Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness LP quarterly 13F filing. The thread reconstructs what the fund likely trimmed — positions up 100–800%+ where basic risk management or position-structure shifts apply — versus what it held firm, where a structural procurement lock-in or an early-innings thesis argues against selling. The overarching frame is Aschenbrenner's anti-consensus discipline: he invests in physical bottlenecks, not consensus chip plays, and holds until the thesis breaks rather than until the stock runs.

ticker_nvda.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ticker_nvda.blurb: NVIDIA designs graphics processing units (GPUs) and system-on-chip products. Originally a gaming chip company, it became the dominant supplier of AI accelerators — chips that perform the parallel matrix math required to train and run large language models. Its H100, H200, and Blackwell GPU families are the de facto standard for AI training infrastructure at hyperscalers and cloud providers. NVIDIA's CUDA software ecosystem creates deep switching costs: virtually all AI frameworks and models are optimised for CUDA, making competing hardware difficult to adopt at scale. NVIDIA also sells networking (InfiniBand, Ethernet) and data-centre systems.
ticker_nvda.recent: NVIDIA reported FY2026 (ending Jan 2026) revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65% YoY, with data centre revenue reaching $186 billion. The company's forward P/E of ~17.5x on 34.8% projected EPS growth produces a PEG of 0.50 — unusually cheap for what is arguably the most critical infrastructure company in the AI buildout. Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) collectively committed over $200 billion in AI infrastructure capex for 2026, the majority flowing through NVIDIA's supply chain.

ticker_avgo.name: Broadcom Inc.
ticker_avgo.blurb: Broadcom is a diversified semiconductor and infrastructure software company formed through a series of acquisitions, most recently VMware (closed 2023). Its chip portfolio spans networking ASICs (custom chips for hyperscaler AI clusters), enterprise storage controllers, WiFi silicon, and set-top-box processors. Broadcom's AI networking chips — particularly its Tomahawk Ethernet switching ASICs and custom AI accelerators built for Google, Meta, and Apple — have made it a second-tier AI infrastructure beneficiary behind NVIDIA. The VMware acquisition added high-margin enterprise software revenue that meaningfully improved the company's margin profile.
ticker_avgo.recent: Broadcom's FY2026 revenue (ending Oct 2026) is on track to exceed $65 billion, with AI-related chip revenue growing rapidly as hyperscalers expand custom silicon programs. Forward EPS growth of 56.3% and a forward P/E of ~23.4x produce a PEG of 0.42 — among the best risk-adjusted valuations in large-cap technology. CEO Hock Tan has guided to $60–90 billion in AI chip revenue by 2027 from three major hyperscaler customers alone.

sources.title: NVIDIA vs TSMC vs Broadcom: AI Chip Stocks 2026 — HeyGoTrade

ticker_be.name: Bloom Energy Corporation
ticker_be.blurb: Bloom Energy manufactures solid-oxide fuel cells — electrochemical devices that convert natural gas or hydrogen into electricity on-site through a chemical reaction rather than combustion, producing lower emissions than conventional generators and requiring no grid connection. The company sells its 'Energy Servers' primarily to data centres, utilities, and industrial customers seeking dispatchable, grid-independent power. Bloom's technology can also run on hydrogen, positioning it as a longer-term clean-energy play as the hydrogen economy matures.
ticker_be.recent: Bloom Energy became one of the defining AI-power stocks of 2025-2026 after Oracle announced it would power its Project Jupiter AI data centre campus entirely with Bloom fuel cells. Q1 2026 revenue rose 130% year-on-year; management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $3.40–3.80 billion and guided adjusted EPS of $1.85–2.25, well above consensus. The stock ran from a 2025 low of approximately $16 to $295 by early May 2026, a gain exceeding 1,700%. Total backlog stands at roughly $20 billion ($6 billion product, $14 billion service). The valuation is extreme: the stock trades at a near-incalculable trailing P/E and analyst consensus price targets (~$180) imply roughly 39% downside, yet the stock continues to attract momentum buyers on the AI-power narrative. Beta stands at 3.83, reflecting the name's status as a high-conviction, high-volatility AI infrastructure speculation.

ticker_sndk.name: SanDisk Corporation
ticker_sndk.blurb: SanDisk was spun off from Western Digital in February 2025 as an independent pure-play NAND flash memory company. It designs and manufactures NAND-based solid-state drives, flash storage chips, and consumer memory products. The spinoff allowed the market to re-rate the business on semiconductor multiples rather than hardware-manufacturer multiples, contributing to an extraordinary post-spinoff rally driven by the NAND supercycle.
ticker_sndk.recent: Since its February 2025 spinoff, SNDK surged over 2,400% through May 2026, reaching an all-time high above $1,189. Fiscal year 2025 revenue was approximately $7.4 billion, with gross margins expanding to ~36% from the low 20s in late 2024, aided by a shift toward high-margin QLC (quad-level cell) products. Analyst targets range from $975 (Wells Fargo, Equal Weight) to $1,250 (Bernstein SocGen, Outperform). A 247 Wall St. analysis in April 2026 flagged potential overvaluation of ~32% versus peers.

ticker_wdc.name: Western Digital Corporation
ticker_wdc.blurb: Western Digital Corporation is a leading American data storage company that designs, manufactures, and sells hard disk drives (HDDs), solid-state drives (SSDs), and flash memory solutions under brands like WD, SanDisk, and G-Technology. The company serves both consumer and enterprise markets, including cloud data centers, and is a key player in the global storage industry. Western Digital has a strong market position in HDDs and NAND flash memory, competing with Seagate and Samsung.
ticker_wdc.recent: In the past 30 days, Western Digital stock has seen positive momentum driven by strong demand for its HDD and SSD products, particularly from cloud and AI data center customers. The company reported better-than-expected fiscal first-quarter earnings in late October 2024, with revenue of $4.1 billion and adjusted EPS of $1.78, beating analyst estimates. Shares rose on the earnings beat and guidance for continued growth in the December quarter.

ticker_intc.name: Intel Corporation
ticker_intc.blurb: Intel is the world's largest semiconductor company by revenue (historically) and the only major chip company that both designs and manufactures its own processors at scale. Its product portfolio spans PC and server CPUs (Core, Xeon), AI accelerators (Gaudi), FPGAs (Altera), and networking silicon. Intel's foundry ambition — Intel Foundry Services (IFS), renamed Intel Foundry — aims to manufacture chips for external customers on its 18A and 14A process nodes, positioning the company as a Western alternative to TSMC. After CEO Pat Gelsinger was replaced in late 2024, the company has undergone significant restructuring.
ticker_intc.recent: Intel reported Q1 2026 revenue of $13.6 billion, up from a depressed base, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.29 versus a near-zero consensus — the beat sent shares up 20%+ in after-hours trading. Data-centre revenue grew 22% YoY. Full-year 2026 EPS estimates of $0.48–$0.56 would represent ~101% growth from the 2025 base — a base-effect figure that reflects restructuring charges and near-zero profitability rather than a dramatic business inflection. Intel trades at ~62.1x forward earnings with a PEG of 0.61 given the distorted growth denominator.

ticker_lite.name: Lumentum Holdings Inc.
ticker_lite.blurb: Lumentum makes the lasers, optical chips, and components that go into the high-speed transceivers wiring AI data centres together. Spun out of JDSU in 2015, it spent its first decade as a 3D-sensing and telecom-optics supplier of moderate growth. The AI-cluster build-out has remade it into one of the principal upstream beneficiaries of hyperscaler capex, alongside Coherent Corp.
ticker_lite.recent: Q1 fiscal-2026 set record revenue, with management citing AI-driven demand and an order book that runs into 2027. In March 2026 Nvidia announced a roughly $2 billion strategic investment paired with multi-year purchase commitments for co-packaged-optics components. The company joined the S&P 500 in March 2026; shares have surged on AI demand, leaving the stock at a forward P/E in the 60s, materially above peers.

ticker_cohr.name: Coherent Corp.
ticker_cohr.blurb: Coherent Corp. (formerly II-VI Incorporated, rebranded after the 2022 acquisition of Lumentum rival Coherent) develops and manufactures engineered materials, optoelectronic components, and laser systems across three segments: Networking, Materials, and Lasers. Its Networking segment — the primary AI data-center play — supplies indium-phosphide chips, transceiver modules, and silicon-photonics sub-assemblies to hyperscalers and networking OEMs. With roughly $5.8 billion in fiscal 2025 revenue, it is one of the largest vertically integrated photonics companies in the world.
ticker_cohr.recent: Coherent joined the S&P 500 in March 2026, the same month it announced general availability of the industry's first dual-laser QSFP28-DCO module — a compact form factor enabling 100G coherent transmission over a single fiber with up to 300 km reach. At OFC 2026 the company showcased an expanded InP portfolio including 400 mW CW lasers, 200G/400G photodiodes, and 800G/1.6T modulators. Fifteen analysts hold an average "Strong Buy" rating with a consensus 12-month price target near $278.

ticker_iren.name: IREN Limited
ticker_iren.blurb: IREN Limited (formerly Iris Energy) is an Australian-founded, NASDAQ-listed company that began as a renewable-energy-powered bitcoin miner and has since pivoted aggressively toward AI and high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure. The company controls significant power capacity — a scarce resource in the AI data-centre boom — across sites in North America, and rebranded from Iris Energy to IREN in November 2024 to signal the strategic shift.
ticker_iren.recent: IREN reported its first profitable fiscal year in 2025, with net income of $86.9 million on $501 million in revenue. A $9.7 billion, five-year cloud-computing agreement with Microsoft was signed in late 2025, calling for deployment of 76,000 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs across 200 megawatts at its Childress, Texas campus. The company targets scaling GPU capacity from 23,000 to 140,000 units through 2026, backed by 2,910 megawatts of renewable power infrastructure.

ticker_corz.name: Core Scientific, Inc.
ticker_corz.blurb: Core Scientific, Inc. provides high-density colocation services and digital asset mining infrastructure in the United States. The company operates through three segments: Colocation, Digital Asset Self-Mining, and Digital Asset Hosted Mining. It offers space, power, cooling, and security services for machine learning and AI workloads, as well as deployment and maintenance of digital asset mining equipment. Core Scientific is a leading player in the Bitcoin mining and AI infrastructure space.
ticker_corz.recent: In the past 30 days, Core Scientific reported earnings on May 6, 2026. The stock has seen significant volatility, with a 52-week range of $9.77 to $25.17, and a market cap of $7.70 billion. The company continues to benefit from the growing demand for AI and cryptocurrency mining infrastructure.

ticker_cifr.name: Cipher Digital Inc. (formerly Cipher Mining Inc.)
ticker_cifr.blurb: Cipher Digital (originally Cipher Mining) began as an industrial-scale bitcoin miner and pivoted aggressively toward AI and high-performance computing infrastructure. The company rebranded in February 2026 to reflect its strategic transformation away from cryptocurrency toward hyperscaler data-centre hosting, leveraging its power-dense facilities and existing infrastructure relationships.
ticker_cifr.recent: Cipher secured a 15-year, 300-megawatt lease with Amazon Web Services estimated at approximately $5.5 billion in contract value, and a 10-year, 300-megawatt lease with Fluidstack and Google. The company now holds 600 megawatts of contracted HPC capacity. Q1 2026 bitcoin mining revenue was $34.8 million while the company absorbed a wider net loss of $114.3 million as it funds the HPC build-out. Stock rose roughly 300% over the trailing twelve months through mid-2025 before the HPC pivot announcement triggered a near-term sell-off on dilution concerns.

ticker_crwv.name: CoreWeave, Inc.
ticker_crwv.blurb: CoreWeave is a neocloud — a GPU-specialist cloud provider that rents NVIDIA accelerator capacity to AI developers, research labs, and enterprises rather than offering the broad service catalogue of a hyperscaler. Founded in 2017 as a cryptocurrency mining operation and pivoted to GPU cloud in 2019, it operates more than 40 data centres with roughly 250,000 NVIDIA GPUs. Its commercial model is long-term capacity contracts — often three to seven years — which produce a large, predictable backlog but require heavy upfront debt-financed capital expenditure. CoreWeave went public on NASDAQ on 28 March 2025 at $40 per share, valuing the company at approximately $23 billion fully diluted. NVIDIA invested $2 billion in CoreWeave at $87.20 per share in January 2026, cementing the symbiotic relationship between the two companies.
ticker_crwv.recent: CoreWeave reported $5.1 billion in revenue for full-year 2025, up 170% year-on-year, with quarterly revenue reaching $1.57 billion in Q4. Microsoft accounted for approximately 67% of FY2025 revenue. OpenAI has contracted up to $22.4 billion in cumulative commitments, and Meta signed a $14.2 billion agreement through December 2031. Total remaining performance obligations represent roughly 13 years of revenue at current run rates. In April 2026, CoreWeave priced an upsized $3.5 billion convertible senior notes offering and announced a multi-year GPU capacity agreement with Anthropic.
